issues.legal_issue: The statutory protection requiring notice before ejectment applies to a monthly non-agricultural tenancy held for more than one year but less than twelve years.
material_facts: The land was non-agricultural and the tenancy was from month to month.
The tenant had occupied the land for more than one year but less than twelve years when the landlord sought ejectment.
issues.conclusion: The protection in section 9(1)(iii) applies to a monthly tenant who has occupied the land for more than one year. The word “term” in the opening part of section 9(1) refers there to the period of occupation, not necessarily a duration agreed in a contract. Such a tenant may be required to quit only on the anniversary of the commencement of the tenancy and after the prescribed notice.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 9(1)(iii) of the Bengal Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, read with its opening words and clauses (a)–(c), the relevant period is the tenant’s occupation where there is no written lease or no specified term; the context determines whether “term” means a contractual duration or a period of occupation. The reference to the end of a year of tenancy can apply to a monthly tenancy, for which the tenant’s year runs from the commencement of the tenancy. The Court approved the construction in Indian Iron and Steel Co. Ltd. v. Baker Ali (AIR 1961 Cal 515), Sudhindra Nath Roy v. Haran Chandra Mistry, and Narayan Chandra Sen v. Sripati Charan Kumar, and considered the contrasting protections in sections 7 and 8.

rule.if: non_agricultural_tenancy and monthly_tenancy and occupation_over_one_year and occupation_under_twelve_years and ejectment_claim

predicates.non_agricultural_tenancy: The tenancy concerns land that is non-agricultural.
predicates.monthly_tenancy: The tenant holds the land under a tenancy from month to month.
predicates.occupation_over_one_year: The tenant has occupied the land for more than one year.
predicates.occupation_under_twelve_years: The tenant has occupied the land for less than twelve years.
predicates.ejectment_claim: The landlord seeks to eject the tenant from the land.

issues.definition: When a monthly tenant facing an ejectment claim has occupied non-agricultural land for more than one year but less than twelve years, the tenant requires qualifying notice before ejectment.

issues.legal_issue: A termination notice that does not provide the statutory notice period before the applicable tenancy-year end is ineffective to terminate the protected tenancy.
material_facts: The landlord served a written notice in late June 1950 requiring the tenant to quit at the end of December 1950.
The tenancy was a monthly tenancy and the record did not establish its exact commencement date; the landlord’s account books showed that the tenant was on the land in November 1938.
The tenant had occupied the land long enough for the notice protection to apply, and the Court concluded that the notice fell short of the required six months.
issues.conclusion: The notice was ineffective because it fell short of the statutory six months’ notice, and the eviction suit was therefore not maintainable on that notice.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9(1)(iii) of the Bengal Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act requires six months’ written notice expiring with the end of a year of the tenancy. For a monthly tenancy, the relevant year runs from the tenancy’s commencement, so the notice must satisfy the required duration in relation to that anniversary. The Court applied its construction of section 9(1)(iii), consistent with the Calcutta High Court decisions it approved: Indian Iron and Steel Co. Ltd. v. Baker Ali (AIR 1961 Cal 515), Sudhindra Nath Roy v. Haran Chandra Mistry, and Narayan Chandra Sen v. Sripati Charan Kumar.

predicates.ejectment_suit_based_on_termination_noti: The landlord brings an ejectment suit relying on a notice to terminate the tenancy.
predicates.protected_monthly_tenancy: The tenant holds a monthly non-agricultural tenancy that is protected by the statutory notice requirement.
predicates.notice_short_of_required_period: The notice does not provide the required notice period before the applicable end of the tenancy year.

issues.definition: In an ejectment suit based on a termination notice, if the monthly tenancy is protected and the notice is too short, the notice is ineffective.
